bug_semantics: With ownPropertyOnly=true, ordinary scope reads reject prototype-inherited keys in src/context/context.ts:readJSProperty, but sort_natural's property comparator read lhs[propertyString] and rhs[propertyString] directly. JavaScript bracket lookup therefore traversed each item's prototype. An untrusted template author could place chosen own-property probes around a target, observe the rendered sorted order, and refine probe values to recover a prototype-inherited secret through a sorting side channel. The pre-fix sort filter already used Context._getFromScope; the directly vulnerable read was sort_natural's comparator.
flaw_origin: e6f5f1cd853c8f7fd615937024b5dfeb3da39cf8 first added and registered sort_natural in src/builtin/filters/math.ts for issue #132. Its comparator introduced caseInsensitiveCmp(lhs[property], rhs[property]), bypassing the context property-reader abstraction. Later comparator renames, export changes, and the 7dfb620d30f8818685e1cfb8e7492313a0d036ab move to src/builtin/filters/array.ts preserved that direct lookup; ff112a4750f91475e9eccdb301d7a468e895f6ca only renamed the function to snake_case. The ownPropertyOnly security boundary arrived later in 7e99efc5131e20cf3f59e1fc2c371a15aa4109db without routing this pre-existing filter lookup through it.

evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/security/advisories/GHSA-rv5g-f82m-qrvv documents the sort_natural direct-bracket read, ownPropertyOnly bypass, probe-order PoC, affected range <=10.25.3, and CVE-2026-39412; its current rendered 'Patched versions: None' conflicts with the captured bundle, but first-party release and ancestry evidence below establish 10.25.4 as fixed. First-party origin issue https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/issues/132 and release https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/releases/tag/v8.4.0 identify e6f5f1cd853c8f7fd615937024b5dfeb3da39cf8 as the sort_natural feature commit in v8.4.0. `git log -L '/^export function sort_natural/,/^}/':src/filters/array.ts 8f69a0839903d85c7b5c9097e39ecce6ac3eab05`, followed across renames/moves into src/builtin/filters/math.ts, traces the vulnerable lhs[property]/rhs[property] lookup to e6f5f1cd853c8f7fd615937024b5dfeb3da39cf8; its tree diff registers 'sort_natural': sortNatural and adds those reads. `git cat-file -p e6f5f1cd853c8f7fd615937024b5dfeb3da39cf8` gives sole parent 570400ebcc80bc3a327d75744fa1a5df76adb9c1 and the exact human-only object metadata quoted in ai_marker. Direct-parent verification with `git show 570400ebcc80bc3a327d75744fa1a5df76adb9c1:src/builtin/filters/math.ts` shows only the existing math filters: no sort_natural/sortNatural, comparator, lhs[property], or rhs[property]. Tag resolution gives v8.3.0^{commit}=570400ebcc80bc3a327d75744fa1a5df76adb9c1, v8.4.0^{commit}=5adebaa710cdd74af175acf01b00a9b7aedda6d7, and `git tag --contains e6f5f1cd853c8f7fd615937024b5dfeb3da39cf8` begins at v8.4.0, proving the introduction boundary. `git log -S ownPropertyOnly -- src` finds 7e99efc5131e20cf3f59e1fc2c371a15aa4109db, first released in v9.34.0, as the later security-option introduction. At v10.25.3, src/filters/array.ts still has caseInsensitiveCompare(lhs[propertyString], rhs[propertyString]), while src/context/context.ts:138-140 blocks inherited keys through hasOwnProperty when ownPropertyOnly is true; src/liquid-options.ts:193 defaults it to true. The direct fix e743da0020d34e2ee547e1cc1a86b58377ebe1ce has parent 8f69a0839903d85c7b5c9097e39ecce6ac3eab05, exactly v10.25.3^{commit}; its src/filters/array.ts diff removes direct indexing, adds shared generator sortBy, and resolves each property through `yield this.context._getFromScope(...)` before comparison. Its test/integration/filters/array.spec.ts diff adds inherited-secret checks for sort and sort_natural. `git log v10.25.3..v10.25.4` contains direct fix e743da0020d34e2ee547e1cc1a86b58377ebe1ce followed by release commit db4348507e6aa205ab2ba5e3fa273c40767e6764, which is v10.25.4^{commit}. First-party PR https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/pull/869 and release https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/releases/tag/v10.25.4 both state the fix is included in 10.25.4.
reasoning: The causal line is the property lookup inside sort_natural, not the later move or the security fix. The history-following -L trace reaches e6f5f1cd853c8f7fd615937024b5dfeb3da39cf8, where the filter was first implemented and exposed with direct lhs[property]/rhs[property] access. Its immediate parent 570400ebcc80bc3a327d75744fa1a5df76adb9c1 is also tag v8.3.0 and has no such function or lines, while the first containing release is v8.4.0; subsequent commits only preserve, move, or rename the mechanism. ownPropertyOnly was introduced later and protected context-mediated property reads, leaving this comparator as a bypass. Version history then carries the vulnerable lookup through v10.25.3. Direct fix e743da0020d34e2ee547e1cc1a86b58377ebe1ce is immediately after the v10.25.3 tag and routes sort_natural property reads through Context._getFromScope; v10.25.4 contains it and its release notes name the security fix.
